goal: Keep pricing-service's test setup healthy and consistent as the project moves forward.
question: Which test framework should pricing-service standardize on going forward, given that the existing suite, CI workflow, and onboarding docs are already built around pytest?
known_constraints: The project has zero runtime dependencies; test tooling is isolated in the [dev] extra
CI currently runs the suite with the single command 'pytest' after 'pip install -e .[dev]'

environment.size: One production function (pricing.tier_price) and one test module with two parametrized cases

evidence: pyproject.toml declares dev optional-dependencies as ['pytest>=8'] and dependencies = [] (no runtime dependencies).
tests/test_pricing.py imports pytest and uses @pytest.mark.parametrize; it is the only test module in the repository, testing the single function pricing.tier_price.
.github/workflows/ci.yml installs with 'pip install -e .[dev]' and runs 'pytest' on every push.
README.md states: 'All tests run under pytest in CI; the suite and onboarding docs assume pytest.'
No conftest.py, pytest.ini, tox.ini, setup.cfg, or Makefile exists; there is no framework-specific configuration beyond pyproject.toml.
tests/__pycache__ contains test_pricing.cpython-314-pytest-9.1.1.pyc, showing pytest 9.1.1 executed the suite locally under CPython 3.14.
A repository-wide search found no unittest, nose, or mock usage in any source or test file.

alternatives.name: Standardize on pytest (status quo)
alternatives.description: Keep pytest>=8 as the sole test framework already used by the test suite, CI workflow, and onboarding docs.
advantages: The existing test module runs unchanged; parametrize and plain asserts are already pytest-style
The CI workflow (pip install -e .[dev]; pytest) needs no changes
README documents pytest as the assumed framework, so onboarding docs stay accurate
disadvantages: Keeps an external dev dependency in an otherwise zero-dependency project
The team must track pytest major-version changes; the repo already runs pytest 9.1.1 while pyproject requires >=8
assumptions: The service remains a small Python package with a lightweight test suite

alternatives.name: Migrate to Python stdlib unittest
alternatives.description: Rewrite the test suite on Python's built-in unittest module and remove the pytest dev dependency.
advantages: Zero external test dependency; stdlib-supported on every Python version the project targets
No framework version pinning or upgrade churn to maintain
disadvantages: The existing parametrized pytest test must be rewritten as unittest cases (e.g. subTest loops)
The CI workflow and the README/onboarding assumption documented around pytest would need updating
assumptions: The team accepts unittest assert-method style (self.assertEqual) instead of plain assert statements

alternatives.name: Keep pytest and add plugin tooling
alternatives.description: Retain pytest and additionally adopt plugins such as pytest-cov and pytest-xdist as the service grows.
advantages: Keeps the existing suite and CI unchanged while adding coverage and parallel-run capability
Access to pytest's plugin ecosystem as the codebase and test count grow
disadvantages: Grows the dev dependency set beyond the single pytest>=8 entry
Adds CI configuration and maintenance for tooling the current one-function suite does not yet use
assumptions: Test suite size and coverage requirements will grow enough to justify the extra tooling

criteria.name: Compatibility with the existing test suite
rubric: Requires a full rewrite of all tests
Requires a partial rewrite of existing tests
Runs existing tests with minor changes
Runs existing tests unchanged, including parametrize

rubric: Requires rewriting the CI workflow and the onboarding docs
Requires minor CI or documentation updates
Matches the current CI workflow and documented assumptions exactly

rubric: Adds several new dependencies and ongoing configuration maintenance
Adds one external dev dependency with occasional version maintenance

rubric: Minimal extension story; tooling must be hand-rolled

Rich ecosystem of fixtures, plugins, and parallel runners
